notes: Pass rates are identical to iteration-1 (1.0 / 1.0 / 1.0 with-skill; 0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0 baseline) — the RUBRIC.md format change did not regress any of the behaviors verified in iteration-1.

New per-criterion 0-3 scoring format worked cleanly in both with-skill runs: 9 criteria (max 27) and 11 criteria (max 33), both within the new 6-12 target, both with correctly hand-computed percentage-based band cutoffs rather than reused fixed numbers.

Baseline's own instinct in this iteration still didn't converge on the with-skill format: meeting-notes baseline used a 1-5 scale with separate hard-fail gates and no triggering-accuracy criterion at all; vague-idea baseline again skipped producing a rubric entirely despite it being requested.

Interesting variation from iteration-1: this iteration's meeting-notes baseline did include a 'Who Uses It / When It Triggers'-equivalent concept in one case (vague-idea baseline) that iteration-1's baseline lacked — still short of a dedicated Trigger conditions section with near-misses, but a reminder that baseline behavior isn't perfectly deterministic across runs.

with_skill runs remain slower and more token-heavy than baseline, now by a larger margin than iteration-1 (deeper interviews plus the added work of writing 9-11 sets of four-level descriptions) — expected given the wider criteria-count target.
